title: Salmon Fishcakes
subtitle: British baked salmon and mashed potato fishcakes
excerpt: Flaked poached salmon mixed with creamy mashed potato, dill, spring onion, and lemon, shaped into patties, coated in panko, and baked until golden and crisp. A classic British fishcake done simply.
sourceNotes: Fishcakes have been a British staple since the Victorian era, originally a way of stretching leftover fish and potato. The salmon and potato version became particularly popular from the 1980s onward.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before baking. Bake from frozen at 200C for 30 to 35 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Shape and freeze in batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Shape and coat the fishcakes up to a day ahead. Keep uncovered in the fridge to dry out the coating.

content.text: The mashed potato must be dry. Wet mash makes a mixture that is too soft to hold its shape. Cook the potato until it is very floury, then let the steam escape before mashing.
Preheat the oven to 200C. Line a baking tray and drizzle with a little oil.
Combine the mashed potato, flaked salmon, spring onion, dill, lemon zest, and a squeeze of lemon juice in a large bowl.
Season well with salt and pepper.
Divide into 8 equal portions. Shape into round patties about 2cm thick.
Set up three shallow dishes: one with flour, one with beaten egg, one with the panko breadcrumbs.
Dust each fishcake in flour first, then dip in egg, then coat in panko.
Place on the oiled baking tray. Drizzle the tops lightly with oil.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and crisp.
Serve with a green salad and a wedge of lemon.

items.cause: The mash was too wet or the mixture was too warm.
items.fix: Dry the mash well and chill the mixture for 20 minutes before shaping.

items.symptom: Coating came off in the oven.
items.cause: The fishcakes were handled too roughly when turned.
items.fix: Turn once only, gently, using a flat spatula.
